question: Mast cell stabilisers such as sodium cromoglicate are most effective when started at least two weeks before the allergy season begins, as they act by preventing mast cell degranulation rather than reversing it.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. Mast cell stabilisers work prophylactically — they cannot reverse ongoing mast cell degranulation. This is why patients should be counselled to start treatment before the allergy season, not after symptoms appear. For acute symptom relief, antihistamine drops (e.g., olopatadine, which has dual action) are preferred.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Mast cell stabilisers prevent degranulation by blocking calcium influx; they have no effect on histamine already released. Pre-seasonal prophylactic use (2 weeks before expected exposure) is far more effective than starting at the onset of symptoms.
